sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the central part of the Borough of Deal, Monmouth County, from Phillips Av. at the top to Roseld Av. at the bottom and from the western edge, where Highland Av. and Norwood Av. run, east across Ocean Av. to the beach and the Atlantic Ocean. Brighton Av., Parker Av. and Runyan Av. cross the sheet from west to east between them. The blocks west of Ocean Av. are laid out in long rows of narrow numbered lots, most still vacant, with a few frame cottages and stables; the blocks east of Ocean Av. are large oceanfront estates. Owners named on the sheet include J. Seligman, S. Lewis, the Coulton estate, K. Lipper, J. Campbell, G. Sidenberg, M. Wolfe, M. Falkenau, J. Hamerslag, H. Zuckerman and L. Sonneborn west of Ocean Av., and P. Lehman, R. Nathan, H. Goldman and J. Seligman on the ocean side, where H. Goldman's house is drawn in brick; Hartford Cottage and Murphy Cottage stand near Roseld Av. Water pipes with hydrants run along the avenues. The bottom margin reads See Volume Two, and a note at Stratford Pl. says the buildings shown there are also on sheet 3 of volume 2. The sheet belongs to volume 1 of the Sanborn New Jersey coast series, drawn at 120 feet to an inch in 1907; buildings are coloured by construction (yellow frame, pink brick), and most are large summer cottages set in wide lots, each lettered with its owner's name.
notes: Highland Avenue on this sheet has no street of that name in OpenStreetMap today; on sheets 3 and 4 Highland Av. continues Almyr Av. south of Poplar Av.
Volume 2 of the coast series continues the borough south of Roseld Avenue.
Central Deal: Phillips, Brighton, Parker, Runyan, Roseld Avs. from Highland and Norwood Avs. east across Ocean Av. to the ocean. 120 ft. One part. Turned, north to the upper left.

sheet-3-1.description: The right part of sheet 3, east of a heavy dividing line, covers the north-western part of the Borough of Deal from Lawrence Av. at the top to Phillips Av. at the bottom, between Norwood Av., which runs diagonally down the left of the part, and Almyr Av. on the right, which continues south of Poplar Av. as Highland Av. Pleasant Pl. runs from Lawrence Av. to Pearl, and Jerome Av., Pearl and Morgan Av. cross the part from west to east; Poplar Av. runs diagonally across the lower half and Wycoff Av. joins Norwood Av. near the bottom. The tracks of the New York and Long Branch railroad and a trolley trestle cross the top left corner. The upper blocks hold large cottages, among them those of H. Mahr and Leo Speyer and The Cedarcroft, while the blocks south of Morgan Av. are cut into rows of small numbered lots, many vacant, with a few frame houses near Wycoff Av. Water pipes with hydrants run along Jerome Av., Pearl and Norwood Av. The sheet belongs to volume 1 of the Sanborn New Jersey coast series, drawn at 120 feet to an inch in 1907; buildings are coloured by construction (yellow frame, pink brick), and most are large summer cottages set in wide lots, each lettered with its owner's name.
notes: Modern names: Pearl is Roosevelt Avenue; Wycoff Avenue is Wyckoff Street; Highland Avenue is the part of Almyr Avenue south of Poplar Avenue.

Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (right) Norwood Av. to Almyr Av., Lawrence Av. to Phillips Av.; part 2 (left) strip west of Norwood Av., Phillips Av. to Roseld Av., drawn north-up, with the title. 120 ft.

sheet-3-2.description: The left part of sheet 3, west of a heavy dividing line, is a strip of the Borough of Deal along the west side of Norwood Av. from Phillips Av. at the top to Roseld Av. at the bottom, with Brighton Av., Parker Av. and Runyan Av. crossing it and the New York and Long Branch railroad along its western edge. It is drawn with north straight up, while the rest of the volume is turned so that north points to the upper left. The blocks are mostly long rows of narrow numbered lots, nearly all vacant; the main buildings are the works of the N.J. Consolidated Water and Light Co. by the railroad near Brighton Av., drawn in brick, a few frame buildings at the corner of Phillips Av. and Norwood Av., and a pair of houses near Roseld Av. The title of the volume, Borough of Deal, with the scale note and a note on the water pipes, is printed in its top left corner, and the bottom margin reads See Vol. Two. Water pipes with hydrants are drawn along Norwood Av. and the cross streets. The sheet belongs to volume 1 of the Sanborn New Jersey coast series, drawn at 120 feet to an inch in 1907; buildings are coloured by construction (yellow frame, pink brick), and most are large summer cottages set in wide lots, each lettered with its owner's name.
notes: The New York and Long Branch railroad is today the North Jersey Coast Line; its crossing of Roseld Avenue was detected as a control point.

Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (right) Norwood Av. to Almyr Av., Lawrence Av. to Phillips Av.; part 2 (left) strip west of Norwood Av., Phillips Av. to Roseld Av., drawn north-up, with the title. 120 ft.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the northern end of the Borough of Deal from Lawrence Av. at the top to Phillips Av. at the bottom, between Almyr Av. on the west, which continues south of Poplar Av. as Highland Av., and the beach and the Atlantic Ocean on the east, with Ocean Av. running down the sheet about two thirds of the way across. Jerome Av., Pearl, Morgan Av. and Poplar Av. cross from west to east, Morgan Av. and Poplar Av. at a slant in the west. The blocks between Almyr Av. and Ocean Av. hold large cottages, among them those of E. Milius, R. Schiffer, Wm. Levy, J. R. Simon, D. Korn, L. Korn, M. Bamberger, E. Wilson, H. F. Loucheim, N. Erb, E. J. Lemon, C. Minzesheimer and Goldsmith, with rows of small lots in the south-west; the ocean side holds the estates of Isadore Strauss, Simon Guggenheim and H. Seligman. Water pipes with hydrants are drawn along the avenues, and the shore line is drawn along the right edge. The sheet belongs to volume 1 of the Sanborn New Jersey coast series, drawn at 120 feet to an inch in 1907; buildings are coloured by construction (yellow frame, pink brick), and most are large summer cottages set in wide lots, each lettered with its owner's name.
notes: Modern names: Pearl is Roosevelt Avenue; Highland Avenue is the part of Almyr Avenue south of Poplar Avenue.
North Deal: Lawrence, Jerome, Pearl, Morgan, Poplar, Phillips Avs. from Almyr Av. east across Ocean Av. to the ocean. 120 ft. One part.
